clusters.text: What is now a useless piece of space junk was for a long time extraordinarily valuable to the scientific community. Launched on November 20, 2004, Swift was a space observatory equipped with three telescopes. It was designed primarily to detect and study gamma-ray bursts, which are among the most energetic explosions in the universe. Swift would locate these events and transmit their positions to observatories around the world for further study. The observatory was designed to operate for a few years in low Earth orbit, but it far exceeded its expected lifespan, helping to make many important discoveries about the evolution of the cosmos, including the study of supernovas and the destruction of stars by black holes. However, in 2024, increased solar activity heated and expanded the upper layers of Earth’s atmosphere, increasing the drag on the satellite and accelerating its descent. Without a propulsion system capable of correcting its orbit, its days were numbered. In July 2026, NASA launched a special $30 million mission to rescue Swift. A robotic spacecraft called LINK was supposed to drag Swift away from Earth by 150 miles, giving it a higher orbit and thus extending its operational life. Unfortunately, LINK failed. In August, NASA administrator Jared Isaacman explained that the difficulties that led to the mission’s cancellation were due to problems with the spacecraft’s control system, which made it impossible to keep it properly oriented and stable in space. On October 26, NASA announced that Swift was less than 170 miles from Earth’s surface—a very low orbit for a satellite. According to the agency, the telescopes on board could no longer maintain stable observations of their astronomical targets. clusters.text: US voters on Tuesday delivered a stunning rubuke to President Donald Trump and his broader agenda. From Texas and South Carolina to Ohio and Kansas, Democrats broke through Republican strongholds, overturned seats that had remained out of their reach for decades and made history in several states.The scale of the gains was particularly striking in places Trump had comfortably carried in the 2024 presidential election, suggesting that the voter bloc which helped him return to the White House is beginning to fracture.With Democrats projected to take control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate, the midterm results represent one of the most significant political reversals of Trump's presidency. But what exactly drove the resurgence? Was it the economic fallout of his policies, the unpopular war with Iran, or growing voter fatigue with the president himself?Inflation, tariffs and Iran war take centre stageThe economy emerged as one of the biggest factors shaping voters' decisions. Trump returned to the White House in 2024 promising to tackle inflation and improve living standards. However, persistent high prices, tariffs on foreign goods and the economic consequences of the war with Iran appear to have undermined that promise.Nearly nine in 10 voters identified the cost of living as a crucial or major factor in their vote, according to exit polls conducted by SSRS for a consortium of US media organisations. Nearly two-thirds blamed Trump for high prices, while around six in 10 said his policies had made the economy worse.The dissatisfaction extended beyond household expenses. Around three-quarters of voters said they were angry or dissatisfied with the direction of the country, while concerns about government corruption and Trump's conduct also featured prominently.The war with Iran added another layer of discontent, with voters increasingly questioning the administration's priorities as economic pressures mounted. Trump's attempts to shift attention towards Democratic candidates, portraying them as radical or dangerous, failed to displace the issue that mattered most to many Americans: the cost of everyday essentials.The election also became a referendum on Trump himself. Despite repeatedly urging voters to treat the midterms as a verdict on his presidency, the Republican leader ended up making his party's electoral challenge considerably harder.

clusters.text: Spain’s transport minister Óscar Puente resigned six days after a high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 69 people. Puente took responsibility for the second major rail disaster in the country this year. He announced his decision on Tuesday after appearing before lawmakers for several hours to explain the circumstances surrounding the October 28 crash.“A transport minister in a country like Spain cannot remain in office after two accidents of this seriousness in less than a year,” Puente said.Puente said he had decided to step down immediately after the latest accident but had kept the decision private. His resignation comes amid mounting pressure from opposition politicians and railway workers' unions, who had called for him to quit following the disaster.What caused the deadly train collision?The October 28 collision occurred when a high-speed train crashed into another train that had stopped on the tracks. The accident killed 69 people and raised serious questions about safety standards across Spain's extensive high-speed rail network.The chain of events leading to the collision began when a communication system essential to the safety mechanism on the Madrid-Seville line failed. Controllers in Madrid then took charge and authorised a state-operated Renfe high-speed train to proceed, despite another train operated by private company Iryo being stationary ahead.“There was a red signal prohibiting movement, yet the train was authorised to proceed,” Puente said last week. “It is a decision made under inexplicable circumstances.”Second major rail disaster on the same route this yearThe latest disaster was the second major train accident on the Madrid-Seville route this year. In January, two high-speed trains collided near Adamuz, killing 46 people. clusters.text: A 24-year-old runner in the New York City Marathon collapsed and died just two miles from the finish line, despite being in "perfect health, perfect shape", her father has said. Rachel Apa, from Lewisberry, Pennsylvania, was running on Sunday with the Parkinson's Foundation Champions to raise money and honor her grandfather who had the disease, she said in a fundraising page. It was Apa's first marathon, though she was an athlete and had trained for months, father Steve Apa told the New York Times. She died from rhabdomyolysis, a rare condition where muscles break down and poison the bloodstream, which can be brought on by overexertion, her father said. Near mile marker 24, Apa collapsed in Central Park and a bystander performed CPR before race medical staff arrived, race organiser New York Road Runners told the BBC's US partner CBS News. According to a New York Police Department statement, which did not name Apa, she was taken to hospital in critical condition. She died that night. The city medical examiner's office said it is still investigating Apa's cause of death. Around Mile 18, the Times reported that Apa had texted her father "Ow" and then a mile later "Ow ow", before sending the message "final stretch" at the 23rd mile, according to the Times. "We are deeply saddened by Rachel's passing following running in Sunday's race. Our thoughts and sincere sympathies are with her family, friends, and the entire running community," New York Road Runners said in a statement obtained by CBS. Apa graduated with a business degree in 2024 from Pennsylvania's Bucknell University, where she also played field hockey, according to her LinkedIn profile online. Since graduating, she had worked as a product manager at an industrial technology company. Ahead of the race, Apa wrote on her marathon fundraising page how much her grandfather, who she was honoring with the run meant to her. "My grandfather was my role model growing up," she wrote. "He taught me to stay active, push my limits, and embrace challenges, shaping my love for sports and movement." She said he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. "I watched as the disease slowly took away the freedom to move that he once loved so much," she continued. More than 61,000 people participated in this year's New York City Marathon, which for the third year in a row broke the world's record for largest marathon.

The watchOS 27.3 developer beta just dropped earlier this afternoon, and these features are meant to be lived with in day-to-day life. clusters.text: Nobody knows who hacked Europe’s supermarkets. But many are looking to Moscow. Two major cyberattacks on European supermarkets in a matter of weeks have exposed the vulnerability of the EU’s critical infrastructure. Cyber experts are raising the alarm that the attacks may be part of Russia’s ongoing hybrid warfare against Europe. Refrigerators in supermarkets in at least nine EU countries went out of service Monday, in what appears to be a repeat of cyberattacks that hit French stores on Oct. 11-12. Stores in Belgium , Luxembourg , Sweden , Germany , Ireland , the Netherlands , Estonia , Finland and Romania were among those affected, according to local news reports and spokespeople for affected supermarkets. The European Commission’s top security officials will look into the incidents, POLITICO reported Monday, with EU Agriculture and Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen describing the attacks as a “deliberate attempt to disrupt our food supply chain.” Identifying who’s responsible for a cyberattack is a tricky business, mired in uncertainty and couched in gradations of likelihood. Even once the technical work is complete, governments often hold back from formally pinning the blame for political, diplomatic or intelligence reasons. “It is not known who is behind this attack, and it may never be possible to identify them,” a spokesperson for Belgium’s cybersecurity agency said. Still, in the wake of the attacks, many analysts had one culprit in mind: Moscow. Along with Iran, China and North Korea, Russia is considered one of four countries that have most commonly targeted Europe with state-backed cyberattacks. But experts say the patterns and targets in this case exclude the other three. “We strongly believe this activity could be attributed to a Russian state-sponsored threat actor,” said Xavier Bellekens, CEO of cybersecurity firm Lupovis. He said that his company’s researchers have collected data on attacks against decoys — known in the industry as honeypots — that point towards a “state-sponsored group.” The expertise required, such as an understanding of industrial control systems and refrigeration technology, is “not trivial,” Bellekens said. The servers the attackers used to hit the decoys were also used by Russian groups some time ago, Bellekens said. The replication of the attacks is another factor pointing towards Moscow. clusters.text: In announcement geared to schools, tech giant shows how entwined AI is with the world’s most popular website Google just acknowledged that you can’t use Google Search without using artificial intelligence . The search giant announced a slate of new AI products for classrooms and schools on Tuesday as well as more ways for teachers and schools to limit or restrict use of those AI tools. The company said the schools should have control over whether students use AI in the classroom. There’s one catch, though: if a school or teacher blocks the use of Google’s AI features, students won’t be able to use Google Search. “After listening to schools, teachers, leading researchers, and policymakers, we are now updating our approach to controls for Gemini, Gemini Notebook, Gemini in Classroom, and Google Search,” company executives wrote in a blogpost. “Access to these products will be entirely off for K-12 student accounts until school administrators explicitly turn them on.” In a comment to the New York Times , Chris Phillips, Google’s vice-president for education, said that there is no Google Search without AI. “Search and AI are deeply integrated,” said Phillips. A school-wide ban on AI would mean that students “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available”, he told the Times. The Guardian also reached out to Google but did not hear back by publication. To some, the move reads like a penalty for not implementing Google’s AI features. New York City’s mayor, Zohran Mamdani, who recently imposed a one-year moratorium on generative AI tools in city schools through the eighth grade, said Google was exploiting its near-total control of online search. “Google is trying to use its monopoly power to force AI into our public schools,” Mamdani posted on X. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children. Our public schools exist to serve students, not to grow the profit margins of Big Tech.” Lina Khan, former chair of the US Federal Trade Commission, echoed his statement, tweeting that Google was using its monopoly on search to “to coerce schools into adopting AI”. He will become the third Bangladeshi cricketer to feature in the BBL, after Shakib Al Hasan and Rishad Hossain. The 400-plus wicket T20 veteran is set to join the Renegades following his ILT20 commitments, with the franchise viewing him as a replacement for the injured Jason Behrendorff and a key addition to their death-bowling options. "I am looking forward to playing in the BBL for the first time with the Melbourne Renegades. It will be special to play at the MCG and I'm excited to join my teammates and contribute to the team," said Mustafizur. Renegades General Manager Max Abbott, speaking at a Zoom press conference on Wednesday, said the Bangladesh pacer had been on their shortlist from the outset. Behrendorff's unavailability for the entire season due to injury further strengthened their interest in Mustafizur, who offers a similar left-arm bowling option. "We were looking for a death-bowling option for us to really back-end the games. And as we know, there's no one better than Mustafiz playing in that role," Abbott said. He added that Mustafizur's familiarity among Australian cricket fans, coupled with his distinctive variations, would make his arrival an exciting prospect. "I think Australian fans are quite familiar with Mustafiz. He's obviously been playing in World Cups for a number of years now. And with the affectionate nickname of the Fizz that we all know him as, I think there's going to be a lot of excitement, not just because of the profile he has, but also because of the skills he has, very unique to him. He bowls those slower balls and has those skills at the death that nobody else has," Abbott said. Mustafizur is expected to miss the Renegades' opening game in Chennai due to the overlap with the ILT20. The franchise will assess his availability for the second game, depending on how his ILT20 team's campaign progresses. For now, they are planning on having him available for their December 22 fixture against the Sydney Sixers at the SCG. The Renegades have also begun marketing his arrival to Melbourne's Bangladeshi community. A dedicated 'Fizz Bay' section will be set up at the MCG for their home games on January 1 and January 16.

Today, we saw there is still more to do to get to this level. Even sometimes in this match we were close to achieving it. We had chances, but we must be ruthless in the final third. Three-nil maybe was more than we deserved.” This Barcelona team will always give you a chance, a thrilling mix of high-spec possession football and large open spaces behind their own teasingly high line. But Villa never looked like getting their teeth into those tender spots, always held at arm’s length, fists whirling in the space between. Two goals here for Raphinha maintained his numerically superlative start to the season. But Pedri was the real star, producing 69 minutes of elite midfield guile, a footballer who at times like these seems to be tickling you very gently to sleep while someone else sticks the dagger in. This was a significant game for its emotional weight, rather than any real sporting jeopardy at this early meandering stage in the Champions League’s expanded format. For the Villa fans crammed into their pen at the top of the stand it was a chance to register a note of progress for this high-wire, ever-evolving team just by taking part. clusters.text: Luis Enrique has confirmed that Paris Saint-Germain's main objective this season is to retain the UEFA Champions League title for a third successive year. The head coach insists that topping the league phase table and scoring 20 goals in the first four rounds count for little right now. His remarks followed an emphatic 6-0 demolition of hosts Villarreal, the sides meeting at La Ceramica in the fourth round of the European competition's league phase. Asked about his team leading the table and racking up such a remarkable scoring rate, Luis Enrique said: "This does not count for anything. There will only be one champion in the final in Madrid, and our goal is to win the title there. In previous seasons, we were crowned champions of the Champions League without finishing the league phase among the top eight." The PSG boss then turned to his attacking philosophy, explaining that his side refuse to sit back even when games turn difficult. "In football, I have seen teams score three goals in five minutes," he said. "There is no point in trying to defend, you must instead focus on attacking, and had we conceded this number of goals in such a short period, we would have faced the same difficulties that Villarreal faced." He added, as reported by the official website of the Union of European Football Associations, "UEFA" : "This is the approach we try to follow, and if there is one thing the team has shown, it is its ability to be consistent and achieve victories, regardless of the injuries or the stadium we play in." Winning the ball back close to Villarreal's goal, the Spaniard argued, allowed his players to impose their considerable superiority. "We were greatly superior because we were fortunate enough to win the ball back near their goal," he explained. Despite the thrashing, Luis Enrique signed off with warm words for the beaten hosts. "Villarreal are a team I really love," he said. "It is a difficult situation, and I feel sorry for them."

clusters.snippet: AEK Athens have been singing about Real Madrid for more than half a century, thanks to a friendly draw and a forward who also recorded the club’s anthem. The line translates roughly as “And your name became the terror of Real.” Its origins lie in Madrid’s visit to Nea Filadelfeia
clusters.text: AEK Athens have been singing about Real Madrid for more than half a century, thanks to a friendly draw and a forward who also recorded the club’s anthem. The line translates roughly as “And your name became the terror of Real.” Its origins lie in Madrid’s visit to Nea Filadelfeia on May 12, 1965, when the teams drew 3–3. Ferenc Puskás featured for Madrid, but AEK’s Mimis Papaioannou caught the visitors’ attention in that game. Puskás was sufficiently impressed to want Papaioannou at Real Madrid. According to Giannis Lambiris’s report for SPORT24, which reproduced the forward’s recollections from an interview with Kathimerini journalist Christos Kontos, Puskás approached him at a dinner hosted by AEK for Madrid’s delegation. He praised Papaioannou’s ability, told him Madrid would sign him, and offered advice on improving his movement without the ball. Madrid’s interest developed into an offer, but AEK refused to let him leave. AEK recalled his performance in a 2021 anniversary post, describing the match as the inspiration for their anthem. Greek broadcaster Sport FM reproduced the club’s account. Papaioannou later provided the vocals for the recording. According to a Greek publication, in.gr, the song began taking shape in 1965 during a tour of Germany involving the footballer and singer Stelios Kazantzidis. The publication credits Christos Kolokotronis with the lyrics and Kazantzidis with the music, and reports that the anthem was recorded and adopted in 1971. The dates rule out a common assumption that the Madrid reference came from AEK’s better-known European results against them. AEK won 1–0 in Athens in the first leg of their 1985 UEFA Cup tie, before Madrid overturned the deficit with a 5–0 home victory. Their Champions League meetings in 2002 were closer. Madrid recovered from 3–1 down to draw in Athens, while AEK came from two goals behind to earn a 2–2 draw at the Bernabéu.

Gael Monfils is a French former tennis player who said a last goodbye to the Paris crowd on November 3, 2026, after 22 years as a professional. He won 13 ATP titles, reached No. 6 in the world and two Grand Slam semi-finals, and remains the last Frenchman to have played the ATP Finals, in 2016. He spent his final season on a farewell tour, from his last Roland-Garros in May to his last Grand Slam match at the US Open in September, a few days after his 40th birthday. Known as “La Monf”, he was one of the great showmen of his era. Monfils announced in October 2025 that 2026 would be his last season, with the aim of playing until he turned 40 on September 1, 2026. He has been officially retired since October 5, 2026, when he asked to be placed on the International Tennis Integrity Agency’s list of retired players. That listing ruled him out of Lyon and of a final tournament at home in Paris. He linked his decision to his separation from Elina Svitolina, saying he had not been able to train the way he wanted. “I gave everything,” he said in Paris. “I’m really happy, really at peace with everything I was able to do.” The Rolex Paris Masters held a 15-minute ceremony for him on Court Central on November 3, 2026, during its 40th edition. Tournament director Cédric Pioline and French Tennis Federation president Gilles Moretton welcomed him onto court, before the crowd unveiled a giant “Merci Gaël” tifo. Please forgive me".According to her family members, the aspirant had been under mental stress for some time.Also read- Hyderabad NEET aspirant found dead at his residence, suicide suspected over depressionThe incident left the family in shock, particularly, when the victim had reportedly qualified for admission to a medical college and her name had figured in the results of the third round of NEET counselling declared earlier in the day, reports the New Indian expressThe girl, a resident of Trivenipuram locality under the Jhunsi police station area, was preparing for the next cycle of the National Eligibility-Entrance Test (NEET), Deputy Commissioner of Police (City) Sagar Jain said.According to her family, she used to study till 4-5 am and wake up at around 2.30 pm. When she did not wake up by 3 pm on Monday, family members went to check on her and discovered the incident, Jain told PTI.As per latest TOI report, the incident took place when the aspirant went into the room and locked it from inside. Later the family members heard a gunshot. When they managed to open the door, they found her with a gunshot injury and immediately informed the police.DCP City Sagar Jain told TOI, "Prima facie the case appears to be a suicide. During the investigation, it emerged that the girl was reportedly upset as her name did not figure in the final list of candidates selected through NEET UG counselling. A licensed pistol has been recovered from the spot and sent for ballistic and forensic examination. Preliminary evidence indicates that the shot was fired at point-blank range, suggesting it could be a case of suicide. However, we are examining all possible angles and the investigation is underway."Police have sent her body for a post-mortem examination, and further legal proceedings are underway.Also read- Kota: NEET aspirant from Bihar dies after being found unconscious in hostel bathroom

clusters.text: BENGALURU: Bus fares across Karnataka's four state-run transport corporations have been hiked, with the maximum increase in KSRTC capped at Rs 9.BMTC city bus fares have been raised by up to Rs 10, Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh announced on Wednesday, news agency PTI reported.The revised fares will come into effect from Wednesday midnight.The minimum fare on BMTC buses in Bengaluru will increase from Rs 6 to Rs 10, while the maximum fare will go up from Rs 35 to Rs 45.The maximum fare on AC Vajra buses will rise from Rs 75 to Rs 90.Vayu Vajra services to Kempegowda International Airport will cost up to Rs 425, compared with the existing Rs 405, PTI reported."Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra governments too have increased bus fares, so we are also hiking bus fare," Suresh told reporters, citing the rise in diesel prices as a reason for the revision.He said the KSRTC fare hike had been capped at Rs 9. clusters.text: Chhath preparations have accelerated across Ranchi and Bokaro, with civic and district authorities ordering cleaning, lighting, barricading and emergency measures at major ghats ahead of the festival. Ranchi mayor Roshni Khalkho reviewed preparations at six ghats on Tuesday and directed Ranchi Municipal Corporation officials to complete pending civic work. The inspection covered Bans Talab, Nayak Chhath Talab, Chambodha Talab, Swarnarekha Chhath Ghat, Kamlu Talab and Power House Chhath Talab. Khalkho met members of the respective puja committees during the inspection to assess local requirements and address concerns. Officials were instructed to continue cleaning the ghats and approach roads, install changing rooms for women devotees, strengthen barricades in deep-water areas and provide additional lighting wherever necessary. The municipal officials were also asked to identify gaps, deploy staff and resources promptly, coordinate with puja committees and conduct regular inspections. The directions place the focus on both basic access infrastructure and safety arrangements at sites expected to receive large numbers of devotees. In Bokaro, deputy commissioner Ajay Nath Jha and superintendent of police Nathu Singh Meena inspected major Chhath ghats in Chas and Bokaro Steel City amid concern over the slow pace of preparations. Their inspection covered Solagidih Lake, Surya Mandir Ghat in Sector 4, Jagannath Temple Ghat, Sector 9 cooling pond and Garga river Chhath Ghat. At Solagidih Lake, Jha ordered the complete removal of water hyacinth and the deployment of additional workers. He also directed Bokaro Steel Plant management to complete delayed cleaning at the Sector 9 pond before Diwali. The instructions indicate that preparations involve coordination between civic authorities and other institutions managing or maintaining individual water bodies. Officials in Bokaro were told to deploy trained divers, install barricades and safety balloons, arrange ambulances and establish mini control rooms. These measures are intended to provide emergency response capacity at the ghats, particularly at locations with deep water or other identified safety risks. clusters.title: Poor students in Prayagraj forced to sell blood for coaching fees, Congress tells NHRC
clusters.text: New Delhi A Congress delegation led by Rajendra Pal Gautam, the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in-charge for Uttar Pradesh on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) moved the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) seeking intervention into the alleged sale of blood by economically disadvantaged students in Prayagraj and other cities of the State to meet the costs of coaching and hostels facilities. https://www.thehindu.com/topic/indian-national-congress/ https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/uttar-pradesh/ Mr. Gautam, who also heads the party’s Schedule Castes (SCs) department, told reporters that the NHRC Chairperson had assured him the matter would be probed by the rights’ body. In a memorandum, Mr. Gautam cited an investigative report published by a leading Hindi daily between October 25 and 27. According to the complaint, a large number of NEET (National Eligibility cum Entrance Test) and SSC (Staff Selection Commission) aspirants, mostly from rural, low-income farming families, were selling blood to pay coaching fees ranging from ₹1.20 lakh to ₹1.80 lakh per year, often demanded as lump sum, besides hostel and mess charges of ₹3,500 to ₹5,000 per month. The news report found that agents and brokers operating near blood banks approached students. While a patient’s relatives were required to pay about ₹8,000 for blood, the student received only ₹3,500 to ₹4,000, after paying about ₹1,500 as processing charges. “Some students admitted to donating blood two to four times a month, posing serious health risks, including anaemia and weakness,” the Congress leader said. “The BJP government has brought the country to such a state that poor students are selling blood to meet their education expenses,” Mr. Gautam added. Blood banks were not directly involved in commercial dealings, he said, but were aware of the practice outside their premises, and that the commercial sale of blood is illegal in India, where only voluntary unpaid donation is permitted. “The situation amounted to a violation of the right to life, health, and education under Article 21, and reflected systemic failures in the availability of scholarships and affordable hostel facilities,” Mr. Gautam said.
